- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–10 days; reduce forecast by 1–3% to account for mean reversion.
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (e.g., 0.0–0.3) and price is trending upward, model frequently underestimates continuation; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for momentum.
- When sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.3) and price is rising, model often overestimates peak; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent high or use 3-day moving average for smoothing.
- Model tends to lag in early horizon (1–3 days) when sentiment is volatile; use 2-day sentiment average to adjust initial forecast for smoother transition.
- If sentiment turns sharply positive after a negative streak, model often fails to recognize reversal; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to capture sentiment-driven bounce.
